description: EF Core applies all changes of one `SaveChangesAsync` call in a transaction, so they commit together or not at all.
A transaction opened with `Database.BeginTransactionAsync` that groups several saves, bulk updates or Dapper calls into one atomic unit.
EF Core's retry policy for transient failures; with retries enabled, explicit transactions must run inside `CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync`.
The bug where two writers read the same row and the later save silently overwrites the earlier one.
A column that EF Core adds to the `WHERE` of updates and deletes, such as `rowversion` on SQL Server or `xmin` on PostgreSQL.
The exception `SaveChangesAsync` throws when a concurrency token no longer matches, which an API usually maps to HTTP 409.
A single statement such as `Where(p => p.Stock >= quantity).ExecuteUpdateAsync(...)` that checks and changes a value atomically in the database.
